However, it invents specifics: exclusive dashboards, 'a hundred-plus pages of metrics', a basement, and SaaS, which is anachronistic for the 90s. It also adds a first-person 'I' opinion about media relations and offers little reasoning on why press worked.","evidence_B":"Repeats 'In', yielding 'In In the end', a join defect. It is about 105 words in an economical first-person voice. It develops the mechanism: press drove users, a cost racket, and cheaper modern channels. It fabricates the PR firm paying reporters, which contradicts 'reporters liked us', and ends somewhat generically.","comparative_reason":"Both answers contain fabrication. A's errors are numerous: anachronistic SaaS, invented dashboards and metrics, and an invented personal experience. B has a stuttered join and one dubious claim, but it stays closer to the voice and actually develops the paid-press mechanism and its limits."}
